page: Microsoft Azure L16aos_v4 is a storage-optimized virtual machine provisioned on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is driven by a 3.7 GHz AMD EPYC 9V74 processor featuring 16 dedicated virtual CPUs mapped across 8 physical cores with two threads per core. Memory capacity is allocated at 128.0 GB of RAM, providing 8.0 GB per core. The hardware configuration bundles 11,519 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD storage. There are no GPUs present on this instance type, and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included.

Benchmark results highlight solid compute performance, with Geekbench single-core scoring 2,084.0 and stress-ng single-core reaching 3,079.05, placing both in the top 25% tier. Multi-core performance metrics, such as PassMark CPU (26,168.72) and Geekbench multi-core (12,359.0), remain in the middle 50% category alongside Clang software compilation (19,339.0) and Redis SET operations (22.64 million operations/sec). Large-block read memory bandwidth falls into the lower 25% at 36.77 GB/sec, while large-model 70B LLM prompt processing lands in the bottom 10% at 4.44 tokens/sec due to memory-bound constraints.

The dense 11.5 TB local NVMe storage allocation provides qualitative cost efficiency for organizations requiring direct high-capacity disk storage without the supplementary expense of network-attached block devices. The 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio additionally balances high-throughput memory operations with compute density.

The L16aos_v4 is suited for transactional databases, NoSQL engines, distributed data stores, index indexing nodes, and large-scale data ingestion pipelines that need high NVMe disk capacity alongside balanced CPU and memory resources.
